events.continuity_hook: Finalizes the Tucson partner weekend after flights, resort, and rental car were booked but before the outbound travel day.
events.interaction_goal: Decide whether to keep the shifted outbound, tighten the connection and rental-car pickup plan, confirm seating choices, set the Thursday arrival routine, and protect Monday checkout around the afternoon return.
events.scenario_brief: A few days before the Tucson hiking weekend, the airline shifts the Tampa departure later, leaving a tighter but still legal connection before the final leg into Arizona. The foothills resort reconfirms the queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, pool, hot tub evening hours, and fitness room, while noting that one spa area will be closed for Friday morning maintenance. The rental car reservation is intact, but the late pickup window makes the arrival sequence less forgiving if the connection slips. Kara still needs a practical Thursday night plan that does not cut into Friday's first hike.

events.continuity_hook: Opens the next winter teaching episode after the personal Tucson weekend, shifting back to flight timing and reliable room setup for a seminar trip.
events.interaction_goal: Compare Friday outbound options, Monday afternoon return choices, the campus hotel versus the suite property, and the questions the university must answer about setup access, parking permits, and Sunday teardown.
events.scenario_brief: After the Tucson trip and end-of-year course paperwork, a university-affiliated rehab lab in Raleigh asks Kara to teach a Saturday-Sunday pediatric handling seminar in late January. She needs to arrive Friday in time for a 5:00 p.m. lab setup window, and the Sunday course block is scheduled to end around 4:15 p.m., making a Monday return more realistic than flying home Sunday night. A campus-adjacent hotel is convenient but has uneven recent reviews, limited recovery amenities, and unclear mini-fridge details; a better-rated suite property about ten minutes away confirms queen rooms, coffee maker, mini-fridge, fitness access, and an indoor pool, but no hot tub. Weekend campus parking and lab access still need clarification.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Raleigh seminar from comparison to booking once the university clarifies parking, lab access, and materials storage.
events.interaction_goal: Book the Friday outbound and Monday afternoon return if fares hold, reserve the suite hotel with cancellable terms, choose the compact rental, and select a window seat where the seat map allows.
events.scenario_brief: The Raleigh host confirms Friday lab access from 4:30 to 6:15 p.m., weekend parking in a faculty lot, and a locked cabinet for Kara's materials between course days. The Monday afternoon return options are still workable, with one itinerary leaving enough time for a normal checkout and lunch before the airport. The suite hotel keeps the clearer room setup and stronger reviews, while the campus-adjacent hotel still cannot confirm the fridge setup. A compact rental now looks more practical than rideshares because the hotel, campus lab, and quick grocery stop are spread out.

events.continuity_hook: Tightens the Raleigh seminar logistics after booking, with campus construction affecting the daily plan more than the hotel choice.
events.interaction_goal: Map Friday arrival and setup timing, set Saturday and Sunday morning leave times, decide where to fit the grocery stop, and keep Monday checkout aligned with the afternoon flight.
events.scenario_brief: A week before the Raleigh seminar, the university sends an updated campus map because construction has closed the usual visitor drop-off near the rehab lab. The suite hotel reconfirms the queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, and fitness room, but the pool will open late on Saturday after maintenance. The Monday afternoon return remains unchanged. Kara still needs a clean Friday airport-to-hotel-to-lab sequence, morning departure times from the hotel, and a Sunday pack-up plan that does not leave Monday cluttered.

events.continuity_hook: Starts the next larger conference episode after a winter teaching trip, with the room block deadline and presenter schedule driving the first planning comparison.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the official block with the suite hotel, review Thursday outbound and Sunday afternoon return patterns, and list what needs confirmation about presenter check-in, lab teardown, mini-fridge availability, and cancellation deadlines.
events.scenario_brief: After the Raleigh seminar, Kara receives the final speaker schedule for a March pediatric neurorehab conference in San Antonio. She has a Friday panel and a Saturday hands-on lab, so Thursday arrival is needed for presenter check-in and materials drop-off. The official conference hotel block is connected to the meeting space and has solid reviews, queen rooms, coffee makers, a fitness room, and an outdoor pool, but mini-fridges are by request and there is no hot tub. A nearby suite hotel confirms queen studio rooms with coffee maker, mini-fridge, fitness access, pool, and hot tub, but it is farther from the meeting rooms and has tighter cancellation terms. Sunday afternoon return flights to Tampa are available, though the lowest fare leaves late enough to make Monday recovery harder.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the San Antonio conference plan from the hotel-block comparison into a time-sensitive booking decision.
events.interaction_goal: Book the Thursday outbound and Sunday afternoon return if fares hold, reserve the official hotel block with the mini-fridge request noted, confirm cancellation terms, and select a window seat where available.
events.scenario_brief: The San Antonio conference office confirms Thursday presenter check-in from 2:00 to 6:00 p.m., Friday panel room access before lunch, and Saturday lab teardown before the evening reception. The official hotel block can still provide a standard queen room with an in-room coffee maker and a mini-fridge request attached, while the connected location removes two days of rideshares with presenter materials. The suite hotel remains better for recovery amenities but has climbed in total cost and would require more daily movement. A Thursday morning Tampa departure and a Sunday afternoon return are still available at acceptable times.
